# Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

**Why this exists.** A host who is away from 14:00 to 16:00 today must block the whole day,
because out-of-office takes dates only. The product change is to block the hours the host is
away and keep the rest of the day bookable. The course reason: Sprint 1 D4 needs two medium
issues merged per member before the deadline, and #9 (PR #78) is the only other one.

**What is fixed.** Verified 2026-10-07 against `origin/main` at `fbae79557b`. Do not relitigate.

  D2 teammate confirmation is still missing. Build to the six criteria as written.

  (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, model `OutOfOfficeEntry`, with `@@index([start, end])`).

  `endDateOffset` in minutes (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/ooo/outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.schema.ts`).
  The handler rounds to whole days at `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts:33-34`
  (`.startOf("day")`, `.endOf("day")`). Its overlap check (`:110-151`) already compares instants.
- **Stored values look like floating wall-clock times in UTC fields.** The handler adds the
  client's UTC offset, then truncates in UTC (`:33`); it reads back with `.tz(tz, true)` (`:348`);
  the slot code does the same at `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts:219`. Prove this

Exit code 1
Decisions for this issue, made before any code was written. The PR is #85.

1. **Slot engine.** A partial-day entry becomes a busy interval, and `getUserAvailability.ts` subtracts it together with the calendar busy times. Whole-day entries keep the existing per-day "away" map. This is the Design decision in the PR.
2. **Whole day.** An entry counts as whole-day when its stored start is 00:00:00.000 and its end is 23:59:59.999 (`isWholeDayOutOfOffice` in `date-ranges.ts`). The form has an "All day" switch. It is on when an existing whole-day entry opens and off for a new entry.
3. **Near midnight.** When the default end passes midnight, it rolls to the next day and the end date moves with it. At 22:30 the defaults are 23:00 to 02:00 the next day.
4. **The list.** A partial-day entry shows its times ("Oct 9, 2026 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM"). Whole-day entries keep the date-only format.
5. **Redirect.** No change. The redirect switch is disabled in this fork (`hasTeamPlan = false` in `CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx`), so a partial-day entry gets no redirect and no "away" badge on the booking page.
6. **Copy.** The time selects reuse the existing `start_time` and `end_time` strings. Two keys are new: `ooo_all_day` ("All day") and `ooo_end_time_must_be_after_start_time` ("End time must be after start time").

One assumption goes with these: a typed time is a wall-clock time in the host's timezone, stored the same way the dates already are.

1	
2	## What does this PR do?
3	
4	- Closes #6
5	
6	An out-of-office entry used to take dates only. The server stretched it to whole days, so a host
7	with a two-hour appointment had to block the whole day. Now the form has a start time and an end
8	time next to the dates, and the booking page stops offering slots inside that window only. Slots on
9	the same day outside the window stay bookable.
10	
11	**The form.** The dates keep the same picker. Below it, an "All day" switch and two time selects
12	(15-minute steps, in the user's 12 or 24 hour format) are new. A new entry defaults to today, the next
13	full hour, and three hours later. At 16:30 the defaults are 17:00 to 20:00. At 22:30 they are 23:00 to
14	02:00 the next day, so the end date rolls forward. "Today" and "the next full hour" are read from the
15	clock in the host's profile timezone, because that is where the stored times apply. If the end is not
16	after the start, the form shows "End time must be after start time" under the time row and does not
17	save. An existing entry opens with "All day" on when it covers whole days, which every entry made
18	before this change does. Saving it without edits sends no times, so the server rounds exactly as it did
19	before and the stored start and end do not move. The list shows the times of a partial-day entry
20	("Oct 9, 2026 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM") and keeps the date-only format for whole-day entries.
21	
22	**The server.** `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate` accepts two optional fields, `startTime` and `endTime`
23	("HH:mm"). Without them it behaves as before, which keeps API v2 and any older client unchanged. The
24	stored values follow the existing convention: the handler adds the client's offset and keeps the
25	host's wall-clock time in the UTC columns (`outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts`, as before). A time of
26	day is applied to that wall-clock date. An end of 23:59 means the end of the day, as it does for date
27	overrides, so a 00:00 to 23:59 entry is stored like a whole-day entry. An end that is not after the
28	start is rejected with the existing `start_date_must_be_before_end_date` error.
29	
30	**The slot engine.** `getUserAvailability` splits entries by their stored shape. An entry that spans
31	00:00:00.000 to 23:59:59.999 is a whole-day entry and keeps the current path: the per-day map that
32	marks the booker's slots as "away". An entry with a time of day is turned into a busy interval in
33	the host's timezone and subtracted together with the calendar busy times
34	(`getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` in `date-ranges.ts`). The booker shows no "away" badge and no
35	redirect for such a window; the slots are simply absent. The redirect switch is disabled in this
36	fork (`hasTeamPlan = false` in the modal), so nothing can set a redirect from the form in any case.
37	
38	**A DST detail worth knowing.** The existing code reads a stored wall-clock value with dayjs's
39	`.tz(zone, true)`. For a time within a few hours of a DST change that form resolves against the
40	wrong offset: 03:30 on 2026-03-08 in America/New_York came back as 04:30-05:00. Midnight, which the
41	whole-day path uses, is never inside that window. Hours are, so the partial-day path parses the
42	wall-clock string in the zone instead (`dayjs.tz("2026-03-08T03:30:00.000", zone)`), which returns
43	03:30-04:00. The tests cover both 2026 change days.
44	
45	**Known limits.** The times are wall-clock times in the host's timezone (the schedule's timezone,
46	which is the profile timezone unless a schedule sets its own). A host whose browser runs in another
47	zone types the time as it applies at home. Partial-day entries do not show the "away" badge or a
48	redirect on the booking page. API v2 still stores whole days.
49	
50	**Files.** Changed: `date-ranges.ts` (+ test), `getUserAvailability.ts`,
51	`outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.schema.ts`, `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts` (+ test),
52	`CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx`, `OutOfOfficeEntriesList.tsx`, `types.ts`, `en/common.json`
53	(2 strings). New: `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`. 662 lines of code changed, 411 of them tests; 10 code files plus `common.json`.
54	
55	## Design
56	
57	**Decision.** A partial-day entry becomes a busy interval that the availability service subtracts
58	with the calendar busy times. Whole-day entries keep the existing per-day "away" map. The two are told
59	apart by the stored shape of the entry, so no schema change and no migration are needed.
60	
61	**Alternatives considered.**
62	
63	1. Teach the per-day map time ranges, so partial days also get the "away" badge and the redirect on
64	   the booking page. This touches `slots.ts`, `date-ranges.ts`, both booker components that render
65	   the badge, and their tests, on top of the form and handler. It passes the repository's limit of
66	   ten code files per PR, and the booker rendering is a second feature.
67	2. Add `startTime` and `endTime` columns, or a boolean `allDay`, to `OutOfOfficeEntry`. The `start` and
68	   `end` columns are already `DateTime`, so the columns would duplicate information, and a migration
69	   needs the schema-change approval that `AGENTS.md` asks for.
70	3. Store real instants instead of wall-clock values for timed entries. Every reader of the table
71	   (the list, the webhook payload, the availability map) applies the wall-clock convention, so mixing
72	   two encodings in one table would need a flag per row and a change in every reader.
73	
74	**Rationale.** The busy-interval path is the smallest change that makes the booking page correct,
75	which is the point of the issue. It reuses `subtract`, which already removes calendar events from
76	the availability ranges, so the slot edges come from code that is tested and in production. The
77	stored-shape rule keeps every existing entry on the path it used before, which is what criterion 6
78	asks for.
79	
80	**Consequences.** Partial-day entries behave like calendar events on the booking page: no badge, no
81	redirect. Whole-day entries are unchanged. The `isWholeDayOutOfOffice` predicate is the single
82	definition of "whole day", used by the engine and by the list. If a later issue wants the badge for
83	partial days, alternative 1 is the path, and it can be built on top of this change.

````python
"""Join hard-wrapped lines inside Markdown paragraphs and list items.

Usage: python3 -I unwrap.py IN OUT
Leaves blank lines, headings, table rows, HTML comments, rules, quotes and
fenced code untouched. Exits non-zero if the text changed beyond whitespace.
"""
import re
import sys

LIST_MARKER = re.compile(r"^(\s*)([-*+]|\d+\.)\s")
NO_JOIN_PREFIXES = ("#", "|", "<!--", "---", ">", "```")


def is_block_start(line: str) -> bool:
    stripped = line.lstrip()
    if not stripped:
        return True
    if stripped.startswith(NO_JOIN_PREFIXES):
        return True
    return bool(LIST_MARKER.match(line))


def is_joinable_target(line: str) -> bool:
    stripped = line.lstrip()
    if not stripped:
        return False
    return not stripped.startswith(NO_JOIN_PREFIXES)


def unwrap(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    out: list[str] = []
    joins = 0
    in_fence = False
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if line.lstrip().startswith("```"):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            out.append(line)
            continue
        if in_fence:
            out.append(line)
            continue
        if out and not is_block_start(line) and is_joinable_target(out[-1]):
            out[-1] = out[-1].rstrip() + " " + line.strip()
            joins += 1
        else:
            out.append(line)
    return "\n".join(out), joins


def main() -> None:
    src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    with open(src, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        before = f.read()
    after, joins = unwrap(before)
    if before.split() != after.split():
        sys.exit("refusing: the text changed beyond whitespace")
    with open(dst, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(after)
    print(f"joined {joins} lines; {before.count(chr(10))} -> {after.count(chr(10))} newlines; words identical")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

````

> ## What does this PR do?
> 
> - Closes #6
> 
> An out-of-office entry used to take dates only. The server stretched it to whole days, so a host
> with a two-hour appointment had to block the whole day. Now the form has a start time and an end
> time next to the dates, and the booking page stops offering slots inside that window only. Slots on
> the same day outside the window stay bookable.
> 
> **The form.** The dates keep the same picker. Below it, an "All day" switch and two time selects
> (15-minute steps, in the user's 12 or 24 hour format) are new. A new entry defaults to today, the next
> full hour, and three hours later. At 16:30 the defaults are 17:00 to 20:00. At 22:30 they are 23:00 to
> 02:00 the next day, so the end date rolls forward. "Today" and "the next full hour" are read from the
> clock in the host's profile timezone, because that is where the stored times apply. If the end is not
> after the start, the form shows "End time must be after start time" under the time row and does not
> save. An existing entry opens with "All day" on when it covers whole days, which every entry made
> before this change does. Saving it without edits sends no times, so the server rounds exactly as it did
> before and the stored start and end do not move. The list shows the times of a partial-day entry
> ("Oct 9, 2026 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM") and keeps the date-only format for whole-day entries.
> 
> **The server.** `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate` accepts two optional fields, `startTime` and `endTime`
> ("HH:mm"). Without them it behaves as before, which keeps API v2 and any older client unchanged. The
> stored values follow the existing convention: the handler adds the client's offset and keeps the
> host's wall-clock time in the UTC columns (`outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts`, as before). A time of
> day is applied to that wall-clock date. An end of 23:59 means the end of the day, as it does for date
> overrides, so a 00:00 to 23:59 entry is stored like a whole-day entry. An end that is not after the
> start is rejected with the existing `start_date_must_be_before_end_date` error.
> 
> **The slot engine.** `getUserAvailability` splits entries by their stored shape. An entry that spans
> 00:00:00.000 to 23:59:59.999 is a whole-day entry and keeps the current path: the per-day map that
> marks the booker's slots as "away". An entry with a time of day is turned into a busy interval in
> the host's timezone and subtracted together with the calendar busy times
> (`getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` in `date-ranges.ts`). The booker shows no "away" badge and no
> redirect for such a window; the slots are simply absent. The redirect switch is disabled in this
> fork (`hasTeamPlan = false` in the modal), so nothing can set a redirect from the form in any case.
> 
> **A DST detail worth knowing.** The existing code reads a stored wall-clock value with dayjs's
> `.tz(zone, true)`. For a time within a few hours of a DST change that form resolves against the
> wrong offset: 03:30 on 2026-03-08 in America/New_York came back as 04:30-05:00. Midnight, which the
> whole-day path uses, is never inside that window. Hours are, so the partial-day path parses the
> wall-clock string in the zone instead (`dayjs.tz("2026-03-08T03:30:00.000", zone)`), which returns
> 03:30-04:00. The tests cover both 2026 change days.
> 
> **Known limits.** The times are wall-clock times in the host's timezone (the schedule's timezone,
> which is the profile timezone unless a schedule sets its own). A host whose browser runs in another
> zone types the time as it applies at home. Partial-day entries do not show the "away" badge or a
> redirect on the booking page. API v2 still stores whole days.
> 
> **Files.** Changed: `date-ranges.ts` (+ test), `getUserAvailability.ts`,
> `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.schema.ts`, `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts` (+ test),
> `CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx`, `OutOfOfficeEntriesList.tsx`, `types.ts`, `en/common.json`
> (2 strings). New: `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`. 662 lines of code changed, 411 of them tests; 10 code files plus `common.json`.
> 
> ## Design
> 
> **Decision.** A partial-day entry becomes a busy interval that the availability service subtracts
> with the calendar busy times. Whole-day entries keep the existing per-day "away" map. The two are told
> apart by the stored shape of the entry, so no schema change and no migration are needed.
> 
> **Alternatives considered.**
> 
> 1. Teach the per-day map time ranges, so partial days also get the "away" badge and the redirect on
>    the booking page. This touches `slots.ts`, `date-ranges.ts`, both booker components that render
>    the badge, and their tests, on top of the form and handler. It passes the repository's limit of
>    ten code files per PR, and the booker rendering is a second feature.
> 2. Add `startTime` and `endTime` columns, or a boolean `allDay`, to `OutOfOfficeEntry`. The `start` and
>    `end` columns are already `DateTime`, so the columns would duplicate information, and a migration
>    needs the schema-change approval that `AGENTS.md` asks for.
> 3. Store real instants instead of wall-clock values for timed entries. Every reader of the table
>    (the list, the webhook payload, the availability map) applies the wall-clock convention, so mixing
>    two encodings in one table would need a flag per row and a change in every reader.
> 
> **Rationale.** The busy-interval path is the smallest change that makes the booking page correct,
> which is the point of the issue. It reuses `subtract`, which already removes calendar events from
> the availability ranges, so the slot edges come from code that is tested and in production. The
> stored-shape rule keeps every existing entry on the path it used before, which is what criterion 6
> asks for.
> 
> **Consequences.** Partial-day entries behave like calendar events on the booking page: no badge, no
> redirect. Whole-day entries are unchanged. The `isWholeDayOutOfOffice` predicate is the single
> definition of "whole day", used by the engine and by the list. If a later issue wants the badge for
> partial days, alternative 1 is the path, and it can be built on top of this change.
> 
> ## Visual Demo (For contributors especially)
> 
> #### Video Demo (if applicable):
> 
> N/A
> 
> #### Image Demo (if applicable):
> 
> | Entry list with an all-day and a timed entry | End time before start time |
> |---|---|
> | <img width="800" height="600" alt="issue-6-list-two-entries" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83628510-dca0-4aeb-afd8-25d3aa0e3456" /> | <img width="800" height="600" alt="issue-6-end-before-start-error" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19cd2ef5-ecb6-46dc-b6c7-156041d5c9ae" /> |
> 
> **Booking page for 2026-10-09 in Europe/London** with a 2:00pm to 4:00pm entry on that day. The seeded
> `pro` user works 9:00am to 5:00pm. Slots run to 1:30pm, which ends at the leave time, and resume at 4:00pm,
> the return time. Nothing is offered between 2:00pm and 3:30pm.
> 
> <img width="800" height="600" alt="issue-6-booking-page-london" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e444bc1-c9bf-4913-9da8-2e6b32652ae1" />
> 
> All three were captured on this branch against the local dev server, logged in as the seeded `pro` user.
> The Next.js dev-only "Issues" badge in the corner predates this PR (`HANDOFF.md`, Known API facts).
> 
> ## Mandatory Tasks (DO NOT REMOVE)
> 
> - [x] I have self-reviewed the code (A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected).
> - [x] I have updated the developer docs if this PR makes changes that would require a documentation change. If N/A, write N/A here and check the checkbox. N/A
> - [x] I confirm automated tests are in place that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.
> 
> ## How should this be tested?
> 
> - **Environment variables:** none beyond a normal local setup.
> - **Test data:** the seed (`yarn db-seed`). Log in as `pro`. The seeded `pro` user is in
>   Europe/London, so switch the booking page to Europe/London with its timezone selector, or compare
>   against that zone.
> - **Happy path:**
>   1. Open Settings, My account, Out of office, and click Add. "All day" is off. The dates are today
>      and the times are the next full hour in Europe/London and three hours later.
>   2. Set the start time to 2:00pm and the end time to 4:00pm on the next weekday, keep the reason, and click
>      Create. The list shows "Oct 9, 2026 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM".
>   3. Open `/pro/30min`, set the timezone selector to Europe/London and select that day. Slots run
>      up to 1:30pm and resume at 4:00pm. No slot starts between 2:00pm and 3:30pm.
>   4. Edit the entry, set the end time to 1:00pm. "End time must be after start time" appears under
>      the time row, and Save does nothing. Set it back to 4:00pm and the message goes away.
>   5. Create a second entry with "All day" on for a later date. The list shows dates only. Open it
>      for edit: "All day" is on. Save without changes. The stored `start` and `end` are unchanged
>      (compare `select start, "end" from "OutOfOfficeEntry"` before and after).
>   6. Delete both entries.
> - **Walked locally** on this branch against the seed data, as above: steps 1 to 6, with the stored
>   rows checked in `psql` after steps 2, 4 and 5 (2026-10-09 14:00:00 to 16:00:00 for the timed entry;
>   00:00:00 to 23:59:59.999 before and after the unchanged save of the all-day entry).
> - **Automated:**
>   - `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.test.ts` (5 new cases): the stored values for a timed
>     entry, the unchanged round trip of an old entry, 23:59 as the end of the day, a window past
>     midnight, and the rejection of an end that is not after the start.
>   - `date-ranges.test.ts` (8 new cases): the whole-day predicate, the partial-day ranges in
>     America/New_York on a normal day, on both 2026 DST change days, across each transition, and
>     the subtraction from a working day.
>   - `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts` (4 cases, also run by the timezone project):
>     a partial-day entry removes only its window and stays off the away map, the slot that ends at
>     the leave time is offered and the two inside the window are not, a whole-day entry keeps the
>     away map, and a window past midnight blocks both days.
>   - Run them with `TZ=UTC yarn vitest run packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/ooo/outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.test.ts packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.test.ts packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`.

```text
# Sprint 1 Deliverables (CSCI 435/535, Fall 2026)

Sprint 1 runs Sep 22 to Oct 8. All deliverables are due **Oct 8, 11:59 PM**. Sprint 1 is worth **100 points** (10% of the course grade).

## Deliverables

**D1: Sprint Backlog (GitHub Issues)**
- **Points:** 10 (team)
- **Required:** Refine the backlog by adding missing issues, closing invalid or duplicate ones, and decomposing large or XL issues. Estimate and select issues the team can finish in about 2.5 weeks, using story points and planning poker. Give every selected issue a single owner. Create a milestone named `Sprint 1` and attach all selected issues.
- **Per-member minimums:**
  - CSCI 435: at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent story points).
  - CSCI 535 (grad): at least 2 medium issues plus 1 additional small issue.
- **Where:** GitHub. Link the milestone in D6.
- **Suggested pacing:** Specs written and peer-reviewed by Sep 27.

**D2: Requirements Specification**
- **Points:** 20 (individual)
- **Required:** The owner writes or refines the spec before writing any code. Features use a user story ("As a [user], I want [goal] so that [benefit]") meeting the INVEST criteria. Include a user scenario, at least 3 testable acceptance criteria, Out of Scope, and Open Questions. Bugs need Observed Behavior, Expected Behavior, Steps to Reproduce, and Additional Information.
- **Review:** At least one teammate comments on the issue confirming it is clear enough to implement.
- **Where:** GitHub issues. Link in D6.

**D3: Design Decisions**
- **Points:** 7 (individual)
- **Required:** At least one non-trivial design decision per issue, with four fields: Decision, Alternatives considered (at least two), Rationale, and Consequences. The page says "one sentence per field is enough."
- **Where:** A `## Design` section in the issue body, an issue comment, or the PR description. Team-wide decisions go in `docs/sprint1/design.md`. Link in D6.

**D4: Code Changes and Pull Requests**
- **Points:** 36 (individual, aggregated across issues and normalized to 36)
- **Required:**
  - At least one PR per issue, created, merged, and closed. Usually one issue maps to one PR.
  - Link each PR to its issue with `Closes #<number>`.
  - The description explains what changed, why, and how it was tested.
  - New or updated tests for every behavioral change, with the test strategy explained in the PR.
  - CI passes if configured. If not, document manual verification in the PR description.
  - At least one teammate (not the author) reviews using the rubric.
  - Merge before the deadline, then delete the branch.
- **Per-PR scoring (20 points):**
  - Correctly implements D2 acceptance criteria: 6
  - Tests written or updated, strategy explained: 5
  - Description explains what, why, and how tested: 4
  - CI passes or manual verification documented: 3
  - Reviewed using rubric, reviewer comment posted on PR: 2
- **Must be able to explain:** "You must be able to explain every line" in your PR. Reviewers or the instructor may ask at any time. Points are lost if you cannot.
- **Summary:** D6 needs a summary table of PRs.

**D5: AI Logs**
- **Points:** 7 (individual)
- **Location and naming:** `ai-logs/sprint1/<github-username>/`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`.
- **Format:** Full metadata, prompts, and responses with timestamps. Accepted formats are `.md` (preferred), `.txt`, or `.json`. Do not submit `.html`, `.docx`, `.pdf`, or links to private chats. Logs must be captured during the session, not reconstructed afterward.
- **Linking:** Reference logs in an **issue comment**, not the PR description or a PR comment. Each contributor (implementer, reviewer, estimator) posts their own comment. Unlinked or broken references earn no credit.
- **No AI used for an issue:** Post a note in an issue comment. No log file is needed, but the folder must exist.
- **Report:** D6 needs tools used, session count, link to the folder, and 2 to 3 sentences per member.

**D6: Sprint Report**
- **Points:** 10 (team)
- **Format:** `docs/sprint1/report.md` (or `report.pdf` or `report.docx`).
- **Required sections:** Team; Sprint overview; Sprint backlog; Requirements & design; Completed issues; Test strategy; AI tool usage; Release; Risks and retrospective; Sprint 2 plan.
- **Length:** No minimum or maximum. Be specific.

**D7: Sprint Release**
- **Points:** 2 (team)
- **Required:**
  1. Merge all Sprint 1 PRs before tagging.
  2. Use the same base version as Sprint 0. No version bump.
  3. Tag with the `-csci435-s1` suffix (example: `v2.17.2-csci435-s0` becomes `v2.17.2-csci435-s1`).
  4. Write a release description listing features, bug fixes, and improvements.
  5. Create the GitHub release from the tag.
- **Deadline:** Tag pushed by Oct 8, 11:59 PM. Link in D6.

**D8: Reflection Survey**
- **Points:** 8 (individual)
- **Required:** Each member completes the survey individually. It is required for completion. The link is distributed via Blackboard and Zulip.

## Zero-Score and Bonus Rules

- **Minimum bar:** A team with no merged PRs (D4), no sprint report (D6), or no release (D7) receives **0 for Sprint 1**, regardless of other deliverables.
- **Extra credit:** A PR accepted or under active review in the real upstream project can earn up to **3 bonus points per PR**, at the instructor's discretion.

## Code Review Rubric

The reviewer posts this as a PR comment, filling it in during the **initial review pass, before the author revises**. Each criterion is scored 1 to 10 with a one- to two-sentence note:

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness: does the change do what the issue asked? | | |
| Test coverage: are tests present and meaningful? | | |
| Code quality: consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | | |
| Documentation: inline comments and PR description are clear | | |
| AI transparency: if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | | |
| Overall: would you merge this as-is? | | |

- Each student conducts at least one review per sprint.
- Across the semester, each student reviews code from every teammate at least once.
- For follow-up revisions, the reviewer may add a brief update noting what changed.

```text
### Settled: how AI logs are captured (D4)

Syllabus §16: "An AI log is the record of an AI conversation with an AI tool — the prompts,
responses, and tool used. Logs are pushed to the team's GitHub repository rather than submitted
separately, and **referenced from the related GitHub issue**." Separately, "for each issue or
sprint, include a short written rationale (in the pull request description or sprint report)
explaining how AI output was used, especially when a suggestion was modified or rejected."
So the log is the **transcript**; the rationale is a different artifact and lives in the PR/report.

**The authoritative spec is <https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/>** (read 2026-09-14) — not
`ai-logs/README.md`, which only summarises it and links a `docs/sprints.md` that exists on no
ref. Requirements, verbatim where it matters:

- Path `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/`; filename `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`.
  Zach's GitHub login is **`zach-short`** (confirmed via `gh api user`). Tool id for this tool
  is **`claude-code`**; `claude-desktop` is the separate Claude Desktop chat app.
- The log must state **the model/tool used** ("e.g. 'Claude Sonnet 4.5 via Claude Code'"), carry
  **the full prompt and response history**, and for agentic tools **all file edits and commands
  run**. A log with "only your prompts (no AI responses), or that is clearly incomplete" does
  **not** meet the requirement. SpecStory satisfies all three: every agent turn is headed
  `_**Agent (claude-opus-5 <timestamp>)**_`, so the model is stated throughout.
- **Files pasted into a session as context** (images, PDFs, snippets) go in a folder beside the
  log with the same name minus `.md`. Report evidence such as D1 screenshots is *not* session
  context and does not belong there.
- **Each log is referenced from the related GitHub issue** as a comment, one per contributor:

  ```
  | # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
  ```

  with a link to the log file and the contributor's role (Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other). "No AI used." if none. **This is the "link" — it points at the log file,
  and it lives in an issue comment, not inside the log.**
- **At sprint end, run `specstory sync` once more** and copy the sprint's files across; a sync
  is only a snapshot of the session so far.

**SpecStory is installed** (`~/.local/bin/specstory`, v2.10.0) and — importantly — **sessions
that were never launched via `specstory run` can still be recovered**, which the course warns is
otherwise hard after the fact:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
specstory list claude                                  # sessions for THIS directory
specstory sync -s <session-id> --output-dir <dir> --local-time-zone
```

Two gotchas, both verified 2026-09-14:

- **Sessions are bucketed by the directory the session ran in.** A session run inside
  `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` is **not** listed from the repo root — run `specstory list` from
  the same directory the session used, or it looks like the log does not exist.
- **A sync is a snapshot.** Re-run it at the end of a session, or the log stops partway.

**Before committing any transcript, scan it for secrets (R16).** SpecStory redacts by default,
but verify rather than trust: grep the file for the literal values in `.env` and for key shapes
(`ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`, `AKIA`, `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY`). Done for the
2026-09-14 log: zero hits.
```

```text
     1	## What does this PR do?
     2	
     3	- Fixes #9
     4	
     5	Leaving the event type editor with unsaved edits used to throw them away without a word. Now a
     6	click on any link that leaves the editor (the sidebar, the top navigation, or the back arrow in the
     7	header) opens a dialog first. "Save" saves and then goes where the user clicked.
     8	`Don't save and leave` goes there without saving. Escape or the close button keeps the user on the
     9	page with the edits intact. With no edits, or right after a save, links work as before and no dialog appears.
    10	
    11	"Has unsaved edits" is the same signal that enables the header Save button,
    12	`formMethods.formState.isDirty` (`EventTypeLayout.tsx:279`). Issue #10 (#20) made that signal
    13	trustworthy on load, so the dialog and the Save button always agree.
    14	
    15	**How it works.** The App Router has no API for blocking a navigation, and the editor's existing
    16	`useHandleRouteChange` hook only runs after the pathname has already changed. So the new
    17	`useUnsavedChangesGuard` hook listens for link clicks on `document` in the capture phase while the
    18	form is dirty. That listener runs before `next/link`'s own handler, which returns early when the
    19	event is already `defaultPrevented` (`next/dist/client/app-dir/link.js:319` in Next 16.2.3). The
    20	hook stops the click and remembers the destination; the dialog then decides what happens. It lets
    21	a click through when the link opens a new tab (Cmd, Ctrl, Shift or middle click, or
    22	`target="_blank"`), when it points to another site, and when it stays on the same page. The last
    23	case covers the editor's own tabs, which only change `?tabName=` and keep the form state.
    24	
    25	"Save" in the dialog runs the same submit path as the header Save button. It resolves to `true`
    26	only when the update mutation succeeds. If the server rejects the save, the existing error toast
    27	appears and the user stays on the page. If the form is invalid, the user also stays and sees
    28	"Error updating settings".
    29	
    30	**Two changes outside the editor, both small.**
    31	
    32	1. `Shell.tsx`: when `backPath` is a string, the header back arrow is now a real link
    33	   (`<Button href>`) instead of a button that calls `router.push`. A click listener cannot see
    34	   where a button is going, so without this the editor could not guard its own back arrow. The
    35	   destination is unchanged on every page that uses `backPath`. The visible difference is that
    36	   the arrow can now be middle-clicked into a new tab. `backPath={true}` still calls
    37	   `router.back()`.
    38	2. Closing or reloading the tab with unsaved edits now shows the browser's own "Leave site?"
    39	   prompt (`beforeunload`). The browser fixes its wording, and it cannot offer Save.
    40	
    41	**Decided with the issue owner (2026-10-07).** The issue's open question, whether the browser Back
    42	button should open the dialog, is answered **no**. Next 16 reloads the page on Back for any
    43	history entry that lacks its private `__NA` state (`next/dist/client/components/app-router.js:284`),
    44	so guarding Back means writing that private state ourselves. That is fragile across Next upgrades,
    45	and it belongs in its own issue if anyone wants it.
    46	
    47	**Known limits.** Browser Back is not guarded, as above. Navigation started from code rather than
    48	from a link, such as the Cmd+K menu, is not guarded either, because it never passes through a link
    49	click. Links to other sites fall to the browser's own prompt.
    50	
    51	**Files.** New: `apps/web/modules/event-types/hooks/useUnsavedChangesGuard.ts` (+ test),
    52	`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/dialogs/UnsavedChangesDialog.tsx` (+ test). Changed:
    53	`EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` (wiring), `Shell.tsx` (back arrow), `en/common.json` (3 strings). 493
    54	lines of code, 301 of them tests.
    55	
    56	## Visual Demo (For contributors especially)
    57	
    58	#### Video Demo (if applicable):
    59	
    60	<!-- drag in: issue-9-demo.mp4 -->
```

"""Count secret-shaped strings in transcripts without printing any value.

Usage: python3 -I scan_logs.py ENV_FILE LOG [LOG ...]
"""
import re
import sys

SHAPES = {
    "github_token": re.compile(r"gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}"),
    "openai_style_key": re.compile(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"),
    "aws_key": re.compile(r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"),
    "private_key": re.compile(r"BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY"),
    "zulip_invite": re.compile(r"join/[A-Za-z0-9]{12,}"),
    "sprint0_fragment": re.compile(r"[fragment redacted][A-Za-z0-9]{4,}|[fragment redacted][A-Za-z0-9]{4,}"),
    "class_roster": re.compile(r"[team redacted]:|[name redacted]"),
    "stripe_key": re.compile(r"(?:sk|rk|pk)_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}"),
    "bearer": re.compile(r"Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}"),
}


def env_values(path: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    values = {}
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        value = value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        if len(value) >= 8 and not value.startswith("http://localhost"):
            values[key.strip()] = value
    return values


def main() -> None:
    env = env_values(sys.argv[1])
    for log in sys.argv[2:]:
        text = open(log, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
        hits = {name: len(rx.findall(text)) for name, rx in SHAPES.items()}
        env_hits = {key: text.count(value) for key, value in env.items() if text.count(value)}
        print(log.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
        print("  shapes:", {k: v for k, v in hits.items() if v} or "none")
        print("  .env values found (key: count):", env_hits or "none")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

<!-- DESIGN -->
## Design

**Decision.** While the form has unsaved edits, one capture-phase click listener on `document` stops a same-origin link that leaves the editor and opens the dialog, and a `beforeunload` listener covers closing or reloading the tab.

**Alternatives considered.**

1. Use the editor's existing `useHandleRouteChange` hook. It runs only after the pathname has already changed, so it cannot keep the user on the page.
2. Also guard the browser Back button with a `popstate` listener. Next 16 reloads on Back for any history entry without its private `__NA` state, so this means writing private Next state ourselves, which any Next upgrade can break.
3. Put a guard into each navigation component: the sidebar, the top navigation and the back arrow. These are rendered by the shared `Shell`, so every page would carry editor-only code, and a link added later would not be guarded.

**Rationale.** One listener on `document` sees every link on the page, including links added later. It runs before `next/link`'s own handler, which skips a click that is already `defaultPrevented`, so it needs no private Next API.

**Consequences.** Browser Back and navigation started from code, such as the Cmd+K menu, are not guarded. The header back arrow in `Shell.tsx` had to become a real link so the listener can see where it goes. Links to other sites fall to the browser's own prompt.

<!-- TESTING -->
- **Walked locally** on this branch: steps 1 to 8 in headless Chrome against `yarn dev`, logged in as `pro` on event type 12, with 23 of 23 checks passing. Event type 12 was restored through the app's own Save afterwards and checked in `psql`.
- **CI:** lint, type checks and both unit test jobs pass. `Security Audit` fails on critical advisories in third-party dependencies, so `required` fails too. The same two checks fail on #84, #79 and #80, which merged today, and this PR changes no dependency file.

design = additions.split("<!-- DESIGN -->\n", 1)[1].split("<!-- TESTING -->\n", 1)[0]

body = body.replace("- **Automated:**", testing.rstrip("\n") + "\n- **Automated:**")
open(sys.argv[3], "w", encoding="utf-8").write(body)
print("patched")

=================== #19
Allow users to set a custom default landing page after login [OPEN]
## User Story
As a user, I want to customize my default landing page after logging in, so that I can reduce repetitive navigation and immediately access the area of the application I use most (such as Bookings).

## User Scenario
A user logs into the application and is frustrated by always being redirected to the hardcoded Event Types page, as they primarily use the app to check their schedule. They navigate to their account Settings menu and locate a new dropdown for the default home view. They change the selection from "Ev

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A dropdown menu is added to the account settings UI to allow users to change their default home view.
2. The dropdown must include, at a minimum, the options: "Event Types", "Bookings", and "Availability".
3. The selected landing page preference is successfully saved to the user's schema/profile.
4. Upon successful login, the application's post-login routing logic redirects the user to their customized landing page instead of hardcoding the redirect to the Event Types page.

## Out of Scope
- Creating new dashboard views or pages to serve as landing pages (only existing pages like Bookings, Availability, or Event Types will be supported).
- Setting organization-wide or workspace-wide default landing pages (this is strictly an individual user preference).

## Open Questions
- Should newly created user accounts continue to default to the "Event Types" page before they configure this setting?

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Host clicks the edit page for an event and a new option appears called "Reminder notification time"
2. The host should be able to select pre-configured times between 15 minutes and 24 hours.
3. The user is then notified at the selected time out from the event start time

## Out of Scope
- Multiple time selections

## Open Questions
- Should the user be notified when the host changes the notification time out
- If a host initially sets the time to be 30 minutes out from the event, then 31 minutes out from the event, the host changes the notification time to one hour, should the user be notified?
=================== #66
Background Scheduling & Email Delivery [CLOSED]
## User Story
As an event host or attendee, I want a reminder email 24 hours before a booked meeting so I arrive prepared.

## User Scenario
A meeting is booked for Thursday at 2:00 PM. On Wednesday at 2:00 PM, the host and attendee receive a reminder email with start times and location/video links

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Confirmed meetings booked at least 24 hours in advance automatically schedule a reminder to send exactly 24 hours before the start time.
2. The system successfully emails the host and attendees a message containing the event details, their local time, the meeting link,  and reschedule/cancel options.
3. If a meeting is canceled or rescheduled before the reminder triggers, the system automatically removes the pending reminder or updates it to reflect the new start time.
4. Automated tests must verify that reminders are correctly scheduled, updated, canceled, and delivered.

## Out of Scope
- Configurable reminder timings or per-event toggles (fixed at 24 hours for this issue).
- SMS or WhatsApp reminders.

## Open Questions
- Should we send only the 24-hour reminder, or include a 30-minute one?
- Should hosts receive these reminders by default, or only attendees, to prevent inbox noise for busy hosts?

== body
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Note: Cal.diy is a community-maintained open-source project. Contributions here do NOT flow to Cal.com's production service. -->

-This PR restores the frontend UI for Issue #11, which requires a reason when a booking is rescheduled based on the Event Type configuration.

It adds the "Require reschedule reason" setting to the Event Type Advanced settings and connects it to the existing reschedule reason requirement logic. When a reason is required, the reschedule dialog prevents submission until a reason is provided.

This PR also changes the default reschedule reason requirement to `OPTIONAL_BOTH` so existing event types do not unexpectedly begin requiring reschedule reasons.

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Event types can already force a **cancellation** reason. The `CancellationReasonRequirement` enum (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:149`) offers `MANDATORY_BOTH` / `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` / `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` / `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, it is stored on `EventType.requiresCancellationReason` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:287`), and it is enforced in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:157-166`.

Rescheduling has no equivalent. A `rescheduleReason` is collected (`packages/lib/bookings/SystemField.ts:10`, `apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx:23`) but it is always optional — `rg -n "requiresRescheduleReason|RescheduleReasonRequirement"` over the repo returns nothing.

So a host who needs accountability gets it for cancellations and silently loses it for reschedules, even though a reschedule disrupts the same attendee and moves the same calendar. Hosts who run paid or high-demand event types are the ones who feel it.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Mirror the cancellation setting for reschedules:

- a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum and a `requiresRescheduleReason` column on `EventType`, with the same four values and the same default posture;
- a dropdown in Event Type → Advanced, sitting next to the cancellation one;
- validation on the reschedule path that rejects an empty reason, shaped like the check at `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:161-166`;
- the reason surfaced wherever the cancellation reason already is.

### User story

As a host, I want to require a reason when someone reschedules one of my bookings, so that I have the same record of why my calendar moved that I already have for cancellations.

### Rough scope

**Medium.** The whole pattern already exists end to end — enum, column, migration (`packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/`), settings dropdown, validation, and unit tests in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts` — so this is one migration plus a parallel copy of known-good code, not a new design.

### Source

`specs/cancellation-reason-requirement/future-work.md`, which lists "Reschedule reason requirement (same pattern, separate setting)" as work deliberately deferred from that feature.

### Additional context

Intended labels: `type: feature`, `scope: medium`. Nearest existing labels: `enhancement`, `effort:medium`. I do not have permission to apply labels to this repo, so they are recorded here until someone with triage access can add them.

## Review text

### Summary

This PR adds the "Require reschedule reason" dropdown to Event Type, Advanced, next to the cancellation one. It passes the setting to the Request Reschedule dialog, which hides "(Optional)" and disables "Send request" while a required reason is empty. It also changes the default from `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` to `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, in `schema.prisma`, in the existing migration and in `isRescheduleReasonRequired`.

The UI side looks right. The dialog uses the same `isRescheduleReasonRequired` helper as `requestReschedule.handler.ts:84`, so the button and the server agree. The repository select, the bookings query and the update schema all carry the new field. On `1d61ffc112`, lint, type checks and both unit test jobs pass in CI. The two red checks are not caused by this PR: `Check Prisma Migrations` fails because its workflow file is invalid (it fails the same way on #77), and `Security Audit` fails on third-party dependencies.

### Changes requested

#### 1. Do not edit a migration that is already on main

`20260916120000_add_reschedule_reason_require/migration.sql` merged with #36. A database that already ran it does not run it again, so this edit changes nothing there. The column keeps `DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY'`. Also, when that migration added the column, PostgreSQL filled every existing event type with `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`, not with NULL. So the new `?? OPTIONAL_BOTH` fallback never reaches those rows, and their hosts still must give a reason. That is the case this PR wants to prevent.

Please put the old migration back as it is on `main`, and add a new migration:

```sql
ALTER TABLE "EventType" ALTER COLUMN "requiresRescheduleReason" SET DEFAULT 'OPTIONAL_BOTH';
UPDATE "EventType" SET "requiresRescheduleReason" = 'OPTIONAL_BOTH' WHERE "requiresRescheduleReason" = 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY';
```

The `UPDATE` is safe now because nothing on `main` lets a host set this value, so every stored value came from the old default. After this PR merges, that is no longer true.

#### 2. Say why the default differs from #11

#11 asks for "the same four values and the same default posture" as the cancellation setting, and that default is `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`. `OPTIONAL_BOTH` is a reasonable choice, so existing event types do not change behavior. Please put that decision in the PR description with the alternative you did not take.

#### 3. Resolve the conflict and link the issue

The branch conflicts with `main` in `EventAdvancedTab.tsx`. The description also needs `Closes #11`, which the Sprint 1 spec asks for.

#### 4. Add tests and the test strategy

The only test change flips the expectation of one existing test. Please add tests for the new behavior: the dialog disables "Send request" when a reason is required and the text is empty, enables it when there is text, and shows "(Optional)" only when no reason is required. A test that the Advanced tab saves the chosen value would also help. "How should this be tested?" still has the template prompts. Please replace them with the steps you used to check it.
